name: Oreb
title: Midianite Prince
summary: Oreb was one of the two princes (along with Zeeb) over the Midianites who were defeated by Gideon and the Ephraimites. He was killed at the rock that was subsequently named after him—the Rock of Oreb. His defeat became a symbol in Israelite tradition of God's mighty deliverance of his people.

keyEvents.title: The Oppression of Israel by the Midianites
keyEvents.description: The Midianites, including princes such as Oreb and Zeeb, oppressed Israel for seven years and destroyed their crops and livestock.

keyEvents.title: Gideon's Victory over the Midianites
keyEvents.description: Gideon defeated the Midianite army with only 300 men, causing the Midianites to flee in panic.

keyEvents.title: The Ephraimites Capture and Kill Oreb
keyEvents.description: The Ephraimites captured the Midianite prince Oreb and killed him at the rock called the Rock of Oreb. His head was brought to Gideon.

keyEvents.title: Oreb and Zeeb Mentioned as an Example of God's Judgment
keyEvents.description: The psalmist refers to the defeat of Oreb and Zeeb as an example of how God judges his enemies, and asks that Israel's enemies suffer the same fate.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah refers to the defeat at Oreb
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah uses the expression "as at the rock of Oreb" as a picture of God's future deliverance of his people from oppressors.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah on the day of Midian
keyEvents.description: Isaiah refers to the day of Midian as an image of God's victory, where the defeat of Oreb and the Midianites serves as a model for the Messiah's deliverance.
